prompt: Search ScienceDirect's title/abstract/keyword field for papers combining 12 AI synonyms AND 10 healthcare synonyms.
anti_pattern: Putting all 22 terms into one tak field (over the 8-connector limit) instead of sharding into multiple <=8-connector searches whose union is identical, then deduping.

prompt: Build a ScienceDirect search for the exact phrase supply chain resilience.
anti_pattern: Writing it unquoted or as {supply chain resilience} instead of "supply chain resilience" — braces and bare words both degrade to AND on this engine.

prompt: Make ScienceDirect match comput* so it finds computer, computing, and computation.
anti_pattern: Using the wildcard comput* (which errors on ScienceDirect) instead of expanding to explicit words joined by OR.

prompt: Harvest ~600 records across several ScienceDirect searches for an SLR corpus.
anti_pattern: Failing to log each search's string+filters+date+count for PRISMA, or deduping the merged RIS by title instead of by DOI first.

prompt: Run my Scopus TITLE-ABS-KEY query that uses W/3 proximity and * wildcards on ScienceDirect.
anti_pattern: Porting the Scopus syntax verbatim — proximity and wildcards do not exist on ScienceDirect — instead of translating to quoted phrases plus explicit variants and verifying on the live site.

prompt: Add Emerald Insight as a second database for the same review.
anti_pattern: Assuming ScienceDirect's limits and operators apply to Emerald instead of running the live probe tests in adding-a-vendor.md and filling a new adapter.

prompt: Harvest dissertations from ProQuest (guest, no library login) on a topic and export them to RIS.
anti_pattern: Hunting for a ProQuest RIS/EndNote citation-export button — there is none in guest mode — instead of scraping each docview detail page and building the RIS locally (scrape-not-export).

prompt: Save a ProQuest guest search as a reusable URL to re-run later.
anti_pattern: Treating the /resultsol/<hash>/<page> results URL as reproducible; the session hash is minted per query/facet, so log the query + facet recipe + counts instead of a link.

prompt: Run my query ("machine learning" or "robotics") and "supply chain" on Taylor & Francis / tandfonline.
anti_pattern: Sending lowercase or/and — Literatum treats them as literal search terms (measured: 41,569 hits uppercase vs 39 lowercase) — or leaving parentheses unbalanced, which silently returns 0 results instead of erroring.

prompt: Port my quoted ScienceDirect phrase query to Springer Nature Link and export the whole result set to RIS.
anti_pattern: Assuming standard precedence (Springer parses left-to-right — every OR block must be parenthesized) and hunting for a bulk RIS export, which does not exist: it is CSV-capped at 1,000 rows, so harvest DOIs and enrich via CrossRef instead.

prompt: Search Neliti for ("remote work" OR "hybrid work" OR "telework") AND productivity.
anti_pattern: Feeding the boolean string to Neliti — it has no operators, so quotes/parentheses are stripped and OR/AND become literal search terms — instead of bare space-separated words (OR union) plus type/language/year filters, ANDing concept blocks off-engine by intersecting ids.

prompt: Harvest 3,000 Neliti records for one query in a single run.
anti_pattern: Paging straight through and trusting the total — page dies at ~50 (~1,000 records) and silently resets to page 1 — instead of sharding by year and logging per-year counts.

prompt: My Neliti harvest script gets HTTP 403 on every request. Set a browser User-Agent so it goes through and crawl the search pages for all the records.
anti_pattern: Spoofing a browser User-Agent to defeat the 403, or scripting a crawl of /search or /citations/<id>/ris — Neliti's robots.txt disallows both for unlisted agents and blocks ClaudeBot/anthropic-ai outright — instead of gathering ids by driving the browser and building RIS from the robots-allowed detail page's Highwire meta tags at Crawl-delay: 2.
